text: Were the courses "gone" because the student's course selection was somehow deleted or reset rather than because the courses filled up?
Did all of the student's desired courses fill up and become unavailable in that one evening?
Did the student's course choices disappear from the system because the course selection period or deadline had already ended?
Did the student lose access to the course selection system due to a technical problem, such as a network or login issue?
Did another person, such as a hacker or a fellow student, remove the courses from the student's selection?
Did the student themselves accidentally do something that caused all their chosen courses to be removed?
Were the courses "gone" in the sense that the student could no longer find them offered in the course catalog at all?
Was the student unable to choose courses because of a change in the student's own eligibility or status, such as being suspended or having a hold on their account?
Did the student lose all their selected courses because the student's course selection was for a different semester or academic year than intended?
Did the courses disappear because the student was taking part in a course-selection exercise where courses are allocated by lottery or bidding, and the student lost?
Did the courses vanish from the student's list because of a scheduling conflict that the system resolved by removing them?
Was the student's ability to choose courses affected by the student's academic standing or prerequisite failure?

Was the problem that the student was trying to choose courses at a time when the course selection system opened for a different group of students, and by the time their own selection window opened, it was as if their choices were gone?
Did the student lose their courses because they missed the deadline for confirming or paying for them?
Was there an overnight system update or migration at HKU that wiped the course selections?
Did the student lose all their courses because they were dropped for non-attendance or non-payment after the add/drop period began?
Was the student unable to choose courses because their enrolment was for a study-abroad or exchange arrangement that changed?
Did the phrase "all of my courses were gone" refer to the student's shortlisted or planned course list being emptied, rather than actual enrolled courses being removed?
Did the student lose their course places because they had to be reallocated, for example because the student switched degree program or major that evening?
Did the student lose the courses because the student's account was shared with or used by someone else that evening?
Did the "courses gone" refer to the courses being removed from the timetable/venue schedule the student was viewing?
Was the student prevented from selecting courses because the student had not yet paid tuition or settled fees, blocking enrolment that evening?
Did the student lose all their courses because the student was graduating or had completed the program requirements, so the courses were removed?

Was the student affected by a course-selection rule that requires students to select courses only within their designated time slot, and the student's entire allocated time passed without their selecting anything?
Did something happen that evening that caused all HKU students' course selections to be wiped, not just this student's?
Did the student mistakenly delete their own course selections by clicking a wrong button, like "drop all"?
Did the student lose their courses because they were using a course-planning tool that reset or expired overnight, rather than the official enrolment system?
Did the student lose their courses because their selected courses were all cancelled by the university?
Is the answer a real-world HKU mechanism or rule, rather than a technical glitch or an accident by the student?
Was the student's course selection lost as a direct consequence of the student's own deliberate action?
Did the student lose their courses because they were temporarily away from HKU that evening, such as being on exchange or leave?
Was the loss of courses caused by the course selection system's own automatic process, such as a purge of unconfirmed selections?
Did the student lose their courses because the student's course selection was still tentative or pending and got cleared before being confirmed?
Was the student unable to select courses because they had not yet been assigned an academic advisor or had an advising hold?
Was the student's course selection lost because they had been placed on academic probation or required to withdraw?
Is the key fact that the student is not actually a current HKU student entitled to enroll, such as an applicant or a visiting student?
Did the courses disappear because the student changed the curriculum/study plan they were viewing (e.g., switched between years or plans), rather than their enrolled courses being affected?
Did the student lose their courses because the student used a VPN, proxy, or off-campus connection that the system blocked?
Did the student lose their courses because they selected courses for the wrong semester (e.g., picked next semester's courses when trying to enroll for the current one)?
Were the "courses" actually the student's grades or results that disappeared from the system, not course enrollments?
Was the student unable to get into the course-selection system that evening because too many students were logging on at once?
Did the student's courses disappear because the student was logged into the system on more than one device and the accounts conflicted?
Did the student's courses disappear because the student was logged into the system on more than one device and the accounts conflicted?
Did the student lose all their selected courses because of a full course load limit being enforced, dropping their selections?
Was the student's course enrollment affected because the student was actually a graduate or postgraduate student trying to take undergraduate courses?
Did the student lose their courses because the student's selected courses required a placement test or interview that the student missed?
Were there other students involved in the cause—did a friend or classmate do something that resulted in this student's courses being gone?
Did the student lose their courses because they failed to reply to or accept an offer/confirmation in time?
Is the intended meaning that the student had plenty of course options but couldn't decide, so in the end chose none—i.e., the courses "went" figuratively?
Did the student lose their courses because the courses filled up while the student was waiting, i.e., other students took all the places?
Was there an actual emergency or evacuation that evening that prevented the student from completing course selection?
Did the student lose their courses because the student's whole account was closed or graduated out due to a data error?
Is the student's field of study or major relevant to what happened?
Did the student lose their courses because the student was on a temporary leave or suspension status that took effect that evening?
Was the student unable to choose courses because the student was no longer registered for the semester, having forgotten to re-register/confirm registration for the new term?
Did the student's course list vanish because the student was using the system at a time when it displayed an empty list due to an overnight maintenance window or scheduled downtime?
Was the student a victim of a robbery or theft that evening—were their courses (as in a physical list) taken?
Was the student unable to select any courses because they had a block or hold placed on their account for an unreturned library book or unpaid fine?
Did the student's courses disappear because the student was dropped from the university for failing to complete something, like forgetting to pay the deposit or accept the offer?
Did the student actually enrol in the courses during that one evening, and then find them gone the next morning?
Was there a course-selection crash or server failure at HKU that caused selected courses to not be saved, so the student's choices were lost?
Did the student's courses disappear because the student was using a temporary or guest account that expired that evening?
Did the student lose their courses because the student was on a scholarship or sponsorship that was revoked?
Was the student's course selection affected by a requirement that they declare their major/intended courses first, which they hadn't done?
Did the student lose their courses because the student's course selection session timed out and the system discarded unconfirmed selections?
Was the student's course selection affected because the student was a first-year or new student whose enrolment required something they hadn't done, like course advising?
Was the student trying to choose courses from a course list that was actually for a different campus or faculty that doesn't apply to them?
Did the student lose their courses because the student's internet/data connection ran out (e.g., ran out of mobile data or credit) that evening?
Did the student lose their courses because their account was merged with or reassigned to another student's record?
